analysis: Security-relevant change: ClusterConfiguration.validate (ClusterConfiguration.swift head ~175-176, base line 174) used to require `nativeMember == nil` whenever a tensorAssistant was set. That kept speculative decoding, which has no parity qualification, off coordinator-paired (public) clusters. It now allows a tensorAssistant beside nativeMember only if `ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant(for: capability)?.policy == tensorAssistant`. Fail-closed check: a nil declaration makes the optional comparison false, so the rule still throws tensorAssistantServesLocally. The docs (configuration.md lines 1635-1636, and the resource_policy_sha256 row) state this build declares none. Effective behavior is therefore unchanged today, and the new surface activates only when a future build declares a public assistant. Exact-policy equality (depth, inventory SHA, verification) limits what can be accepted. The comparison runs inside the `if let tensorAssistant` block, after the existing checks for Qwen TP, serial prefill and no private images. Docs show the declared policy joined into the resource-policy digest with an evidence SHA, which binds the declaration to the native start. Related threat model entries: T-056 (overclaiming correctness), T-054 and TB-011 (qualification and generation binding). The edits to the refusal text, comments and docs are documentation only, and the message is still within the 240-character limit. Remaining integration questions, outside the supplied source: ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant and ClusterPublicTensorAssistant (who can declare one, and whether evidence is required). Also unverified is whether ClusterApprovalAttachment on the leader and the coordinator-side qualification gate use the same equality check. No regression is identified in the supplied lines.
